When Zendaya appeared at a London photocall on July 17, 2026, her ensemble included a pair of earrings featuring 3,000-year-old gold discs [Zendaya’s Earrings Are Part of a Much Bigger Problem](https://hyperallergic.com/zendayas-earrings-are-part-of-a-much-bigger-problem/). The objects, which have been linked to the Ziwiye hoard discovered in northwestern Iran in 1947, quickly became the subject of online debate regarding the provenance of ancient artifacts in contemporary fashion [claim:public-web:3Jj-I5R0Tea9PYw_u0CmtEKvejXC8AqL4QVjmSa61PY:1, 18, 2].

## The Provenance of Aesthetic Commodities

The earrings consist of ancient gold discs repurposed into 18-karat gold settings [claim:public-web:3Jj-I5R0Tea9PYw_u0CmtEKvejXC8AqL4QVjmSa61PY:4]. According to reports on the assembly of the piece, the discs were acquired by a jeweler and mounted with diamonds, a process that reflects a broader market trend of dismantling and reframing archaeological fragments for luxury jewelry [claim:public-web:3Jj-I5R0Tea9PYw_u0CmtEKvejXC8AqL4QVjmSa61PY:4, 14]. This practice of commodifying antiquity is not isolated to this single instance; similar processes are routinely applied to beads, carvings, and other ethnographic or ritual objects from Egyptian, Phoenician, and Roman contexts [claim:public-web:3Jj-I5R0Tea9PYw_u0CmtEKvejXC8AqL4QVjmSa61PY:13, 14].

## Performative Display and Archaeological Erasure

Critics and archaeologists have pointed to the incident as an example of how the fashion industry leverages exoticism to drive engagement, often overlooking the history of the objects involved [claim:public-web:3Jj-I5R0Tea9PYw_u0CmtEKvejXC8AqL4QVjmSa61PY:6, 7]. When ancient artifacts are permanently altered—through drilling, cutting, or mounting—their ability to provide scientific or historical information is often compromised [claim:public-web:3Jj-I5R0Tea9PYw_u0CmtEKvejXC8AqL4QVjmSa61PY:16, 17]. Unlike restoration efforts, which seek to preserve an object's integrity for future research, this repurposing is typically a one-way transformation that severs the item from its original context [claim:public-web:3Jj-I5R0Tea9PYw_u0CmtEKvejXC8AqL4QVjmSa61PY:17].

## Institutional Fragility and Global Markets

The controversy arrives amid ongoing international tension and reports of cultural heritage destruction in various regions, including Iran [claim:public-web:3Jj-I5R0Tea9PYw_u0CmtEKvejXC8AqL4QVjmSa61PY:10]. Following the public reaction to the jewelry, forensic archives and advocacy groups launched a petition requesting transparency regarding the provenance of the discs [claim:public-web:3Jj-I5R0Tea9PYw_u0CmtEKvejXC8AqL4QVjmSa61PY:9]. The case highlights a systemic disconnect in the art and fashion markets, where the desire for high-status, ancient materials frequently outpaces the demand for verified ownership or archaeological clearance [claim:public-web:3Jj-I5R0Tea9PYw_u0CmtEKvejXC8AqL4QVjmSa61PY:15, 20]. As these objects continue to circulate in private collections and luxury retail, the process of documenting their history remains as fragmented as the artifacts themselves [claim:public-web:3Jj-I5R0Tea9PYw_u0CmtEKvejXC8AqL4QVjmSa61PY:20].
